newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end week at new high, eye rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end week at new high, eye rate cut.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended at a new record high on Friday, supported by expectations for a possible fresh official rate cut next week, dealers said.
Weakness on Wall Street did not soften Madrid shares, although it suggested a cautious approach, and some took profits before the close, they added.
The general Index ends up 5.83 points, or 1.11 percent, to 531.68 and the Ibex-35 gained 63.1 points, or 1.04 percent, to 6,128.07.
Telefonica underperformed the market, adding 30 to 3,910, as did as Repsol which gained 20 pesetas to 5,980.
Endesa, after Thursday's announcement of an eight percent fall in 1Q profit, gained just 10 pesetas to 10,680.
"The trend's still very positive. The trading volume is heavy, and stocks are shooting higher," a dealer said.
Volume hit a record high in the year with more than 120 billion pesetas shares changing hands.
Dealers stressed positive expectations for April CPI, seen breaking the two percent level year-on-year, prompting hopes for the Bank of Spain's fourth key money market rate cut this year.
